content.topic: character consistency and motion transfer with Kling / AI video tools
content.audience: AI creators, agencies and operators building repeatable characters

analysis.first_two_seconds: Starts with a tool update and high-value promise: maintain character consistency and copy motion from reference videos.
analysis.hook_line_or_visual_summary: The format promises to test whether a new motion-control/character-consistency feature is worth using.
analysis.narrative_shape: tool update -> availability warning -> setup requirements -> step-by-step setup -> tests/results -> practical tips
scene_beats: show final AI character outputs and dancing/motion examples
explain that consistency requires multi-angle character images
generate front/side/back/smile references with an image tool
upload reference video and character image into Kling
create an element from the character images
describe the character or use automatic description
give troubleshooting tips for bad imports and camera movement
analysis.camera_behavior: mix of AI output clips, screen recordings and creator/tool tutorial visuals
analysis.cut_rhythm: medium-fast, tool-demo pacing; visual change every 5-10 seconds
analysis.subtitle_style: native vertical captions plus occasional labels/tool UI text

analysis.proof_mechanism: shows multiple generated character outputs, reference motion examples and UI screens
analysis.cta_style: educational; likely invites commenting for guide/prompt

transcript_assisted.quality_note: Local faster-whisper tiny transcript. Good enough for summary, not for exact quotes.
transcript_assisted.corrected_summary: The video explains that a motion-control/character-consistency feature can transfer movement from a reference video while keeping the same AI character. It recommends generating multiple character images from different angles, including at least one smiling with teeth, then uploading reference video and character images into Kling/Elements. It warns that some platforms may not expose the newest feature yet, and gives troubleshooting tips: re-export reference videos if Kling errors, match the first frame/posture of the reference, and avoid videos with too much camera movement.
key_takeaways: Character consistency needs a 360-style reference set, not only one image.
A smiling-with-teeth reference matters because teeth can break consistency.
The reference video's first frame/posture should match the character image for better results.
Some aggregators may lag behind official model features.

workflow_extracted.name: Consistent AI character with reference motion
steps: Define the character identity and visual constraints.
Generate front, side, back and smile/teeth references.
Choose a stable reference motion video.
Match character pose to the first frame of the reference video.
Create a reusable character element/profile in the video platform.
Generate test outputs in several scenes.
Reject outputs with face/teeth/body drift before client delivery.
workflow_extracted.onia_use: Build reusable ONIA/client avatars for demos, explainers and UGC without relying on a new face prompt every time.

usable_patterns: tool-test framing: 'probe esto para ver si sirve'
explain hidden setup steps that beginners miss
include troubleshooting tips, because that creates trust
turn character consistency into a client-safe production checklist
best_for: UGC-style business videos with approved characters
onia_adaptation.sample_onia_hook: La razon por la que tus videos IA cambian de cara en cada escena no es el modelo: es tu sistema de referencias.
onia_adaptation.sample_higgsfield_prompt_block: Create a vertical AI video tutorial showing a clean ONIA workflow for keeping one approved character consistent across scenes: reference board, front-side-back-smile images, stable motion reference, character profile, test grid and final approved clip. Spanish captions, screen/UI overlays, no copied creator identity.
onia_adaptation.adaptation_notes: Very useful for ONIA production quality. Convert it into an internal checklist and client-safe explanation instead of influencer-body content.

not_useful_or_use_with_care: Influencer/body-focused examples are not the ONIA business angle.
Avoid content that looks like deepfake or unauthorized likeness cloning.
Do not promise perfect consistency; present it as a controlled workflow with review.
Avoid copying public reference motion if it is recognizable or copyrighted.
notes: High operational value for ONIA because it explains why character consistency fails and how to systematize it.
